record.paper_title: Selected open problems in Matching Under Preferences
record.original_question: For max smti, the problem of finding a maximum-cardinality stable matching in a Stable Marriage instance with ties and incomplete lists, close the gap between the best known lower and upper bounds on the approximation ratio in the unrestricted case.

evidence.quote: These upper and lower bounds for general max smti remain the best known to date, and it is an open problem to close the gap between them.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A Stable Marriage instance with Ties and Incomplete lists (SMTI) consists of two disjoint finite sets $U$ (men) and $W$ (women). Each $u \in U$ has a preference list that is a weak linear order (a total preorder, i.e., ties are permitted) over some subset $A(u) \subseteq W$ of acceptable women, and symmetrically each $w \in W$ has a weak preference order over some subset $A(w) \subseteq U$, with $u \in A(w) \iff w \in A(u)$. A matching $M$ is a set of mutually acceptable man–woman pairs in which each person appears at most once. A pair $(u,w)$ with $u \in A(w)$ that is not in $M$ is a blocking pair of $M$ if (i) $u$ is unmatched in $M$ or strictly prefers $w$ to his $M$-partner, and (ii) $w$ is unmatched in $M$ or strictly prefers $u$ to her $M$-partner. A matching is stable if it has no blocking pair. MAX-SMTI is the problem of computing a stable matching of maximum cardinality.

Let $\alpha^*$ denote the infimum, over all polynomial-time algorithms $A$ for MAX-SMTI, of the worst-case ratio $|\mathrm{OPT}(I)|/|A(I)|$ over instances $I$ (the approximation ratio). Determine $\alpha^*$, or equivalently, close the gap between the best known polynomial-time approximation upper bound and the best known inapproximability lower bound for MAX-SMTI in the fully general (unrestricted) setting.
artifact.status_search_result: The general MAX-SMTI problem still has a gap between the best known polynomial-time approximation ratio of 3/2 (Király, McDermid) and the best known NP-hardness lower bound of 33/29 (≈1.1379), with a UGC-based lower bound of 4/3. No improvement to either bound in the unrestricted case has been reported; recent progress (e.g., 25/17 algorithms, 5/4 tight bounds) concerns restricted variants (one-sided ties, ties at the end of lists). The problem appears to remain open as of 2026.

status_evidence.title: A Tight Approximation Bound for the Stable Marriage Problem with Restricted Ties
status_evidence.snippet: Best approximation 1.5 for general MAX-SMTI; tight 5/4 result only for the restricted-ties variant.
status_evidence.claim: General MAX-SMTI upper bound remains 3/2; improvements are for restricted variants only.

status_evidence.title: A 25/17-Approximation Algorithm for the Stable Marriage Problem with One-Sided Ties
status_evidence.snippet: Approximation ratio 25/17 obtained for the one-sided-ties variant, not the unrestricted case.
status_evidence.claim: Improvements in approximation ratio below 3/2 are restricted to special cases of MAX-SMTI.

status_evidence.title: Hardness and Approximation Results for Some Variants of Stable Marriage Problem
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work continues to focus on hardness/approximation in restricted variants of MAX-SMTI.
status_evidence.claim: Active research continues without closing the unrestricted MAX-SMTI gap.
